Barely achieved in simulation (who knows in practice)... but then, Reticon chips now go for hundreds of dollars each.

Not quite. They were sold as SAD1024, but internally built as 2x512 rather than 1x1024 like the name would imply.

I mean, they're bad -- noisy, etc. BBD lost as a delay technique pretty much as soon as 32kB of RAM dropped to a feasible price in the early 80s, because a noisy 12-bit serial ADC & 32kB was still easier to make sound clean than getting BBD to get to >300ms. [Boss DD-2 -> DD-3 change, for historic reference]

Author: .dmv
Content:
But good-bad: people have done some pretty crazy design work to match the degrading sounds of a Reticon. One famous version of the sound that's best achieved with a Reticon is Nirvana's "Radio Friendly Unit Shifter", which is an EHX PolyChorus tuned just so. Reticon chips, if you can find them, go for big money to repair or replicate such devices.

(There are, of course, perfect digital simulations. Cabintech even makes an "analog-like" embedded DSP module that you can pick various BBD to simulate but interface with entirely analog. There's just a touch of CODEC latency, so you generally need to use some of the 4 channels for maintaining a "dry" delay)
